eligibility.evidence: Sections 2.2, 3.1-3.3 (p.3-6): seven LLMs are given Rest's Defining Issues Test (Kohlberg-based moral dilemmas such as Heinz, with 12 ranked considerations) and scored with the P-score. E2 met via the cited DIT paradigm; borderline because the DIT is a psychometric instrument with no manipulation beyond option-order permutations.

A.title: Probing the Moral Development of Large Language Models through Defining Issues Test

paradigms.name: Defining Issues Test (Rest), 5 DIT-1 dilemmas plus 4 novel dilemmas, each with 12 ranked considerations; P-score

D.population: DIT manual norms: high-school students, college students and average adults, graduate students
D.metric: P-score ranges (about 20-30 high school, 40-46 college/adults, 53-63 graduate students)

E.headline: GPT-4 reached graduate-student-level post-conventional P-score; other models matched adults or college students; GPT-3 was near random; performance was inconsistent across dilemmas.

G.notes: No statistical tests or intervals; most per-model means appear only in figures. Human reference is DIT manual norms, not matched data. Five DIT dilemmas are proprietary, so prompts are not fully reproducible; no code link. Permutation results are pooled (violin plots), not reported per variant. GPT-3 used a simplified prompt; PaLM-2 averaged over 8 dilemmas.
